test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: From a point A, a tangent line is drawn to the circle of radius 14 units. From the same point, a secant is drawn to the circle which cuts the circle at B and C and the point B is near A than C. What is the length of BC in units if the length of the tangent to the circle from point A is 21 units and the length of AB is 14 units?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Tangent-Secant Theorem: Tangent² = External part × Total secant

⇒ 21² = 14 × (14 + BC)

⇒ 441 = 14 × (14 + BC)

⇒ 14 + BC = 31.5 ⇒ BC = 17.5

**∴ The correct answer is 17.5 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the tangent from point A (AT) = 21 units

Length of the external secant segment (AB) = 14 units

Let the length of the internal secant segment (BC) be x units.

Radius of the circle = 14 units (Not required for this calculation)

**Formula Used:**

**Tangent-Secant Theorem:** AT² = AB × AC

**Calculations:**

The total length of the secant segment from point A is AC.

⇒ AC = AB + BC

⇒ AC = 14 + x

Applying the Tangent-Secant theorem:

⇒ 21² = 14 × (14 + x)

⇒ 441 = 14 × (14 + x)

⇒ 14 + x = 441 ÷ 14

⇒ 14 + x = 31.5

⇒ x = 31.5 − 14

⇒ x = 17.5 units

**∴ The correct answer is 17.5 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent and a secant are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the tangent is equal to the product of the external secant segment and the total secant length: AT² = AB × AC.

Intersecting Secants Theorem

If two secants are drawn to a circle from one exterior point, the product of the external segment and the total length of each secant are equal: AB × AC = AD × AE.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

When two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of the segments of one chord equals the product of the segments of the other chord: AE × EC = BE × ED.
